First, we find the constant $B.$ Multiplying both sides of the given equality by $(x+1)({x}^{2}+20)$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}-5x-27 & =(2x+B)(x+1)-({x}^{2}+20).\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $x=0$  into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{0}^{2}-5(0)-27 & =(2(0)+B)(0+1)-({0}^{2}+20) \\ -27 & =B-20 \\ B & =-7.\end{aligned}
$$

 

We now integrate this function term by term, adding the constant of integration at the very end.

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{{x}^{2}-5x-27}{(x+1)({x}^{2}+20)}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{2x-7}{{x}^{2}+20}-\frac{1}{x+1})\text{d}x \\  & =\int \frac{2x}{{x}^{2}+20}\,\text{d}x-7\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+20}\,\text{d}x-\int \frac{1}{x+1}\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

For the first integral, we use the substitution ${x}^{2}+20=u.$ Then, $2x\,\text{d}x=\text{d}u,$ and we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{2x}{{x}^{2}+20}\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{1}{u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡|u| \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+20).\end{aligned}
$$

For the second integral, we use the fact that $\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+{a}^{2}}\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{a}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{x}{a}),$ which results in

$$
\begin{aligned}7\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+20}\,\text{d}x & =7\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+(2\sqrt{5})^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =7\cdot \frac{1}{2\sqrt{5}}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{x}{2\sqrt{5}}) \\  & =\frac{7\sqrt{5}}{10}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{\sqrt{5}x}{10}).\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, for the third integral, we get

$$
\int \frac{1}{x+1}\text{d}x=\operatorname{ln}⁡|x+1|.
$$

So, we get the following result:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{{x}^{2}-5x-27}{(x+1)({x}^{2}+20)}\,\text{d}x & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+20)-\frac{7\sqrt{5}}{10}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{\sqrt{5}x}{10})-\operatorname{ln}⁡|x+1|+C\end{aligned}
$$
